prompt.context: Our client is Great Burger (GB), the fourth largest fast food chain worldwide by number of stores. GB competes head-to-head with McDonald's, Wendy's, Burger King, and KFC, offering food and combos for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. GB owns some stores but operates primarily under a franchising model: 85% of stores are owned by franchisees who pay a franchise fee and manage day-to-day operations, while GB controls major decisions such as menu and store appearance. As part of its growth strategy, GB has analyzed potential acquisition targets including Heavenly Donuts (HD), a growing doughnut producer with US and international store presence. HD also operates under a franchising model, but franchises areas or regions rather than individual restaurants — franchisees are required to open a certain number of stores within their territory. GB's CEO has hired McKinsey to advise on whether GB should acquire HD.
prompt.question: What areas would you want to explore to determine whether GB should acquire HD?

clarifying_info.q: How large is GB's current store network?
clarifying_info.a: GB has 5,000 stores total: 3,500 in North America, 1,000 in Europe, 400 in Asia, 100 in other regions.

clarifying_info.q: How large is HD's current store network?
clarifying_info.a: HD has 1,020 stores total: 1,000 in North America, 20 in Europe, none in Asia or other regions.

clarifying_info.q: What are GB's and HD's current financials?
clarifying_info.a: Refer to Exhibit 1 which will be shown during the case.

clarifying_info.q: What is the doughnut market size?
clarifying_info.a: Doughnut consumption per capita in the US is $10 per year today, projected to grow to $20 per year in 5 years. US population is approximately 300 million.

exhibits.title: GB and HD Key Facts and Financials
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of GB and HD across store counts by region, annual growth in stores, total store sales, parent company revenues, and key expense line items as a percentage of sales, plus profit margin and sales per store versus industry average.

exhibits.title: Sales and Profitability Per Store
exhibits.shows: A table showing per-store unit volumes, prices, and margins for GB's existing products and hypothetical HD doughnut sales within GB stores, along with a cannibalization rate.

framework: Stand-alone value of HD: assess doughnut market growth, HD's historical and projected sales/store growth, competition landscape, profitability margins, and capital required to fund continued expansion
Synergies and strategic fit: identify revenue synergies (cross-selling, geographic expansion) and cost synergies (SG&A integration, purchasing scale, property/equipment leverage)
Brand fit: evaluate whether brand quality is compatible, degree of customer overlap, and whether co-marketing would enhance or dilute both brands
Management and cultural fit: assess capabilities of HD's top and middle management, cultural compatibility, and likelihood key talent would be retained post-merger

Ability to execute the merger: review GB's prior M&A and integration experience, and examine whether the different franchising structures (individual stores vs. area franchising) can be managed simultaneously

questions.prompt: What areas would you explore to determine whether GB should acquire HD?
questions.guidance: A strong answer structures exploration into: (1) stand-alone value of HD — market growth, HD revenue and profit trajectory, competitive position; (2) synergies — revenue upside from cross-selling and geographic expansion, cost savings from SG&A consolidation and purchasing scale; (3) strategic and brand fit — customer overlap, brand compatibility; (4) management and cultural fit; (5) integration feasibility — GB's M&A track record and the complexity of running two distinct franchise structures simultaneously.

questions.prompt: What potential synergies can you think of between GB and HD? (Refer to Exhibit 1)
questions.guidance: Revenue synergies: sell HD doughnuts in GB stores or selected GB products in HD stores; leverage GB's international footprint to help HD expand outside North America; use GB's superior store-location skills (GB sales/store of $1.1M vs. industry average of $0.9M) to improve HD store selection (HD at $0.7M vs. industry average of $0.8M); accelerate HD store openings with GB's stronger balance sheet and capital access. Cost synergies: biggest opportunity is corporate SG&A — HD's G&A is 15% of sales vs. GB's 8%, suggesting meaningful consolidation potential; some food-cost savings on overlapping ingredients (beverages, frying oil); potential to leverage GB's lower property and equipment cost ratio (4.6% vs. HD's 8.5%) through superior lease negotiation.

questions.prompt: The team thinks synergies can double HD's US market share in 5 years, and that GB's capital access allows HD's store count to grow by a multiple of 2.5. What sales per store will HD require in 5 years to achieve these goals?
questions.guidance: Work through the calculation step by step: derive current HD US market share from total store sales and the US market size; double that share applied to the projected market size gives target HD sales; divide by the projected store count to get required sales per store. A good candidate notes the answer implies less than doubling same-store sales, which is reasonable given per-capita consumption is projected to double.

math.setup: Current HD sales = $700M (from Exhibit 1, approximately all US given 1,000 of 1,020 stores are in North America). Current US doughnut market = $10/capita x 300M people = $3B. Current HD market share = $700M / $3B ≈ 23%, round to 25% for simplicity. US market in 5 years = $20/capita x 300M = $6B. Target HD US sales = 25% share x 2 (double) x $6B = $3B. Target HD store count = 1,000 US stores x 2.5 = 2,500 stores. Required sales per store = $3B / 2,500 = $1.2M.
steps: HD sales target (double share) = 25% x 2 x $6B = $3B
math.answer: $1.2M per store — less than double current HD sales/store of $0.7M, which is reasonable given per-capita consumption is projected to double

questions.prompt: How would you assess the profitability impact of selling HD doughnuts in GB stores?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers two parts. Basic profitability analysis: incremental revenue = number of doughnuts sold per store x price per doughnut x number of GB stores; incremental costs = cost of goods, incremental labor, employee training, software changes, incremental marketing, and distribution costs if not produced in-house; incremental investment = possible space expansion or store layout changes for in-house doughnut production. Cannibalization: quantify rate at which doughnut sales displace existing GB sales (higher at breakfast than lunch/dinner); use historical cannibalization data from prior GB product launches; also consider cannibalization of nearby HD standalone stores (compare HD sales performance when competitor opens close by).

questions.prompt: What would be the incremental profit per GB store if HD sells 50,000 doughnuts per store at $2 per doughnut at 60% margin, with a 10% cannibalization rate on GB sales? (Refer to Exhibit 2)
questions.guidance: Incremental profit equals HD contribution minus the contribution lost to cannibalized GB sales. If only Question 3 was completed (or time is short), the interviewer may skip this and state the answer is $15K.

math.setup: Incremental profit = (HD units x HD price x HD margin) – (GB units x cannibalization rate x GB price x GB margin)
steps: Cannibalized GB sales = 300,000 units x 10% = 30,000 units
Lost GB contribution = 30,000 units x $3 x 50% = $45,000

questions.prompt: You run into the CEO of GB in the hallway. He asks you to summarize McKinsey's perspective on whether GB should acquire HD. What would you say?
questions.guidance: A strong synthesis leads with a clear recommendation, supports it with the key quantified finding, flags remaining work, and closes with integration considerations. Structure: recommendation (early findings suggest the acquisition would create significant value); key evidence (e.g., $15K incremental profit per GB store from selling HD doughnuts, implying ~$75M across 5,000 GB stores globally or ~$50M for North American stores where HD brand is established; plus unquantified revenue and cost synergies); open items (full quantification of synergies and investment required to set a fair acquisition price); integration plan (managing different franchise structures, cultural alignment, and capturing synergies).

math.setup: Rough total synergy from doughnut cross-sell: $15K/store x 5,000 North American GB stores ≈ $50M incremental annual profit (North America only, where HD brand presence exists)
steps: $15K per store x ~3,500 North American GB stores ≈ $52.5M, roughly $50M
math.answer: ~$50M in incremental annual profit from doughnut cross-sell in North American GB stores alone

brainstorming.prompt: What cost synergies could GB capture by acquiring HD?

categories.name: Corporate SG&A
ideas: Shared HR, finance, legal, and IT systems

categories.name: Procurement and food costs
ideas: Combine purchasing volume on shared ingredients (beverages, frying oil)
Negotiate better supplier contracts using combined scale

categories.name: Property and equipment
ideas: Apply GB's superior lease-negotiation skills to HD store expansion
Share real estate expertise and site-selection capabilities

categories.name: Marketing and brand
ideas: Shared advertising spend or combined media buys
Leverage GB's marketing infrastructure for HD brand

categories.name: Technology and systems
ideas: Combined loyalty or mobile app platform

recommendation: Early evidence suggests GB should acquire HD — the acquisition would create significant value through both revenue and cost synergies
The most quantifiable near-term synergy is selling HD doughnuts in GB stores, generating approximately $15K incremental profit per store and ~$50M annually across North American GB stores
risks: Different franchise structures (individual restaurants vs. area franchising) may be complex to manage simultaneously
Cultural misfit between the two organizations could result in management departures and loss of HD institutional knowledge
Cannibalization of nearby HD standalone stores could partially offset revenue synergies
HD's current sales per store ($0.7M) is below industry average ($0.8M), suggesting execution risk in store-level economics
next_steps: Quantify the full range of revenue and cost synergies to set a fair acquisition price
Develop an integration plan addressing franchise structure alignment and cultural integration
Assess GB's balance sheet capacity and financing structure for the deal
Conduct due diligence on HD management team and franchisee relationships
